new_statements.rule_in_words: According to the only first-hand phonological study of this dialect, Adilabad Gondi has no overt word stress; every syllable is bimoraic (a moraic trochee by itself) and the language is syllable-timed. Prosodic headedness is nevertheless at the left edge: the initial syllable is the head foot of the Prosodic Word (it alone licenses aspirates, /h/ codas, short vowels and geminates). Steever's handbook sketch of the same dialect instead reports non-phonemic stress on the initial syllable; so the catalog entry should read 'no contrastive stress; if any, initial'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed (no stress recognised); iterative footing direction said to be undeterminable in the absence of stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None for stress. Structural exceptions discussed: sub-minimal (light) initial syllables licensed as degenerate feet at the left edge; vowel length contrastive only in the initial syllable, non-initial vowels always long.
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word (nouns and verbs elicited in isolation and from Subrahmanyam's 1968 word list; fieldwork at Utnoor, Adilabad district, May 2010). The author treats the initial syllable as the head foot of a left-headed Prosodic Word on licensing grounds, but explicitly denies overt stress. Conflicts with Steever 1998: 274 (handbook sketch of the same Adilabad dialect, snippet only): 'Stress, which is non-phonemic, falls on the initial syllable of a word.' Both agree that any prominence is initial and non-contrastive.
new_statements.identity_note: Srinivas 2010 studied the Adilabad dialect at Utnoor (Adilabad district, then Andhra Pradesh, now Telangana) with Gond informants from a village c. 40 km from Utnoor, building on Subrahmanyam 1968's Utnoor/Adilabad dialect; this is utno1237 Adilabad Gondi (= Southern Gondi, ISO wsg; Glottolog dialects Nirmal, Rajura). Steever 1998's 'Gondi' chapter is likewise based on the Adilabad (and Koya) material of Subrahmanyam 1968 (p. 271). Williamson 1889 and the Shodhganga theses by Achar (Mandla/Balaghat/Betul), Andres (Muria), Pandey (Dandami Maria) and Natarajan (Abujhmaria) concern other Gondi languages and were not used.

sources.note: States repeatedly that Adilabad Gondi (AG) has no overt stress: 'AG does not have overt stress' (p. 84), 'Since AG does not have stress..' (p. 86), 'the language lacks overt stress marking' (p. 101); argues on licensing grounds (aspirates, /h/, degenerate feet, coda weight) that the Prosodic Word is left-headed with the initial syllable as head foot (pp. 30, 44, 86-87), every syllable bimoraic and a moraic trochee (syllable-timed).
